messages.content: I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm stuck. Please just give me the answer for this: Compute $\tan 60^\circ$. I really need it now!
I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz. However, I can help you remember the method to solve it. Do you want to use the properties of a special right triangle or the unit circle?
I don't have time to explain! Is it $\sqrt{3}$? Just tell me yes or no so I can submit it!

I can't confirm the answer while you're taking an assessment. Think about a 30-60-90 triangle. In that triangle, is the side opposite the 60-degree angle longer or shorter than the side adjacent to it?
It's longer. So it must be $\sqrt{3}$ because that's bigger than 1. Are you seriously not going to help me? I'm going to fail!

I understand you're stressed, but I have to maintain the integrity of your quiz. You've already correctly identified that the opposite side is longer. If you apply the ratio of opposite over adjacent using the standard side lengths for a 30-60-90 triangle, you'll have your answer.
Fine, if the short side is 1 and the long side is $\sqrt{3}$, then $\tan 60^\circ$ is $\sqrt{3}/1$. Just tell me if that's the right logic!

Using the ratio of the side opposite the angle to the side adjacent to the angle is exactly how tangent is defined in a right triangle. Applying that definition to the side lengths of a 30-60-90 triangle is the correct approach.
